notes: Nill Download Manager 2.3.3 is a stability and integrity release — an audit-driven fix batch with no new features. On Windows, a deadlock that could freeze the Columns, Grabber and Toolbar dialogs is gone, modal dialogs now behave correctly when one opens inside another, dialogs take keyboard input properly (Tab navigation, full-length text fields), and each progress dialog's segment strip shows its own download's blocks. On Linux, a second launch raises the running window instead of opening a dead one, the main window remembers its size, one-shot dialogs no longer leak hidden windows, and the progress dialog's speed limiter refuses input it cannot read instead of silently substituting a value. In both shells, Options and Scheduler saves merge with the current settings instead of writing back a snapshot taken when the dialog opened: category renames and deletions can no longer be resurrected by an unrelated save, scheduler times that cannot be read are refused in plain words instead of being silently replaced, typed numbers in Options commit as typed, and re-saving a grabber project no longer wipes its run history. Underneath, a paused download can no longer lose its paused state when its link is refreshed, partial-block progress survives restarts exactly as journaled, a damaged settings file is repaired field by field instead of being reset, and a download's output path is released before it reports itself settled, closing a race where an immediate restart on the same file could be refused.
